judgements.skipSteelman: The defect is real and dated, and the doneCriterion is genuinely provable: 995bb52 (2026-09-08) deleted .claude/ship-bar.md and left CLAUDE.md:67 pointing at it, and that commit staged .claude/settings.json (a non-.md file), so the pre-commit suite DID run on it — a path-resolution test would have gone red on the exact commit that shipped the defect. That is more than most candidates can say. Instruction rot also has a second, independent witness (harness-evolution-1 / JClaw 0dfcd451), so the class recurs in a repo that reviews harder than this one. A ~25-line, zero-dependency, sub-100ms check that turns a prose claim into a compiled one is the cheapest kind of gate this repo builds.
judgements.bittenUsEvidence: REAL BUT ZERO-COST, MEASURED. The false line lived 9 days (2026-09-08 -> 2026-09-17). I searched for a single session it misled and found none: (1) `git log --all -- .claude/ship-bar.md` returns exactly 3 commits (15a7f08 create 2026-07-11, 00f28c7 sync 2026-09-07, 995bb52 delete 2026-09-08) and NOTHING after the deletion — nobody tried to open, recreate or edit the named file. (2) The one session that did work in this exact area, 45114a0 on 2026-09-14, ran a machine-wide ship-bar investigation (6-case matrix over ~/.claude/new-project.sh, found its settings.json was invalid JSON, CORRECTED a wrong memory claim) and got the right answer — it was not misled by CLAUDE.md:67, six days after the line went stale. (3) RESUME_HERE.md:95, the other always-loaded file, already carries the TRUE state: 'new-project.sh now skips the project ship-bar when the global hook exists'. (4) `grep -n ship-bar docs/sessions/-SESSION-LOG.md` -> 6 hits, none of them a session hunting for a missing file. (5) The false part of the line is the PROVENANCE only — the operational claim ('per-turn ship-bar contract auto-injects') is TRUE, it just injects from ~/.claude/settings.json. An agent reading the line behaves correctly and is wrong only about where the text came from. Measured cost of the defect to date: zero incidents in 266 commits / 3 months.

standingCost.secondsPerCommit: AS PROPOSED: reads 1415 lines across 6 files (RESUME_HERE.md alone is 991) + ~130 stat() calls — still well under 1s, so seconds are NOT the objection. The real timing defect is WHEN it runs: the hook's docs-only fast path (.githooks/pre-commit:20-26) exits 0 before vitest whenever every staged file matches \.md$. 87 of the last 266 commits (32.7%) took that path, and 61 of those 87 touched RESUME_HERE.md or a CLAUDE.md — i.e. 70% of the skipped commits edited exactly the files this gate reads. The gate is structurally blind on the commit that introduces prose drift; its red then lands on the NEXT source commit, which did not cause it. Broken attribution on a blocking gate is the canonical --no-verify trigger. Note .claude/ship-bar.md itself ends in .md: had 995bb52 not also staged settings.json, the real defect would have sailed through too.
standingCost.tokensPerTurn: Every gate this repo has shipped bought itself an always-loaded CLAUDE.md block: chaos = 8 lines (42-49), claimcheck = 11 lines (50-60). CLAUDE.md is 5153 bytes / 756 words / 74 lines ~= 18 tokens per line. A gate with an exemption POLICY to explain (6 noise classes, a WILL-CREATE allowlist, a cross-repo base map, a count floor) is an 8-10 line block ~= ~180 tok/turn, every turn, forever, on a repo already at ~6.7k tok/turn. The scoped version needs 2 lines ~= ~35 tok/turn. The irony is load-bearing: a gate against stale prose is paid for in new always-loaded prose that can itself go stale.
standingCost.linesToMaintain: AS PROPOSED: ~80-120 lines of test + extractor, PLUS a suppression set that is re-litigated against a file rewritten 164 times a quarter. RESUME_HERE.md is 991 lines, carries 84 unique backticked path tokens, is committed 164 times in 3 months and CLAUDE.md:70 mandates it be 'rewritten, never appended to' — its entire token set churns every session. SCOPED VERSION: ~25 lines, zero suppressions, over 4 files totalling 156 lines that changed 9 times in 3 months.
standingCost.newFailureModes: (1) FALSE REDS DOMINATE, MEASURED BY ME: my own naive extractor (backticked, contains '/', no spaces, no http, no glob) over the 6 instruction files gives 132 tokens, 24 unresolved, of which exactly ONE is the defect — 23 false to 1 true, 4.2% precision. The brief's own stricter filter measured 16 unresolved / 1 real = 6.25%. 19 of my 24 false reds are in RESUME_HERE.md, which contributes ZERO true ones. The noise is the repo's own writing idiom, not sloppiness: angle-bracket templates (`src/core/npc/<Name>.ts`, `tests/<slice>.plants.ts`, `src/config/og<Name>.ts`), brace shorthand (`src/{core,config,game}/CLAUDE.md` — correct and useful), npm specifiers (`@types/node`), a CIDR block (`192.168.68.0/24`), a schemeless GitHub URL, AS3 tag lists (`<questdata>/<skilldata>/<npcdata>`), enum shorthand (`EQ_HAIR/HEAD/NECK/SCABBARD`), memory slugs (`combat-core/crit-1.3-is-sealed-...`), run-scoped fragments (`run2/`, `run11/`), sibling-repo paths (`harness/chaos/`, `harness/workflows/`) and 2 WILL-CREATE inputs. Shipping green requires suppressing SIX distinct classes. (2) THE SUPPRESSION LIST IS A HIDING PLACE, and the prompt's question 'where does 10 exemptions go in six months' has an answer on the tree TODAY: the class 'bare relative fragment' must swallow `core/`, `config/`, `game/`, `run2/`, `run11/` — so a genuinely deleted directory named in prose as `docs/loop/` is byte-indistinguishable from the idiom and passes silently. The gate would then report 0 over a live defect, which is precisely the claimcheck false-pass this repo already paid 82 corrections for. (3) THE COUNT FLOOR IS A SECOND COPY OF A VALUE. The proposal's 'carry a count floor so a broken extractor cannot pass' means every prose edit that adds or removes a path token must also move a number in a test file — on a doc-heavy repo with 87 md-only commits a quarter that is a pin that drifts, i.e. the repo's own 'two copies of one value' killer, installed deliberately. (4) CLEAN-CLONE RED. Resolving `~/...` and `harness/chaos/` against $HOME and a named-sibling-repo map makes a repo test depend on checkouts outside the repo. This repo explicitly practises clean-clone green (commit 'SESSION23 A11.5 wrap: clean clone green'); the proposed base map breaks it on any machine without ~/kheshav-code/agent-harness.

judgements.simplerVersion: TWO STEPS, and step 1 ships regardless of whether step 2 ever does. STEP 1 (one line, zero maintenance, available now): fix CLAUDE.md:67 to name the real source, `~/.claude/settings.json` (its UserPromptSubmit hook cats ~/.claude/ship-bar.md). That is the entire remediation of the entire measured defect. What the gate buys over it is detection of the NEXT occurrence — and that has to be priced honestly: the class has fired ONCE in 266 commits, at zero cost, and the gate is skipped on the 33% of commits most likely to cause it. STEP 2 (the only version that earns its place, ~25 lines, ZERO exemptions): scope the check to the four STATIC instruction files — CLAUDE.md, src/core/CLAUDE.md, src/config/CLAUDE.md, src/game/CLAUDE.md (156 lines total, 37 path tokens, 9 commits in 3 months) — and resolve REPO-ROOT-RELATIVE tokens only: no $HOME, no sibling-repo map, no WILL-CREATE allowlist, no count floor. Measured on today's tree that set has exactly FOUR unresolved tokens: the real defect, plus `core/`, `config/`, `game/` at CLAUDE.md:29-30, which are layer names in the dependency-direction rule. Eliminate those three by PROSE PRECISION, not suppression — write `src/game/` may import `src/core/` + `src/config/`, which is also strictly more accurate. Result: 4 files, 37 tokens, 0 unresolved, 0 exemptions, and a test whose pass condition is 'every one resolves'. EXCLUDE RESUME_HERE.md and docs/research/HARNESS.md explicitly and say why in the test header: RESUME_HERE is a session scratchpad rewritten 164 times a quarter that owns 19 of the 24 false reds and none of the true ones — policing it is how this gate becomes the thing people bypass.
judgements.why: The gate AS PROPOSED does not survive its own numbers: 4.2% precision on today's tree, six suppression classes on day one, a count floor that is a self-inflicted drifting pin, a base map that reds a clean clone, and — decisive — it is skipped by the docs-only fast path on 32.7% of commits, 70% of which edit the very files it reads, so its red arrives on somebody else's commit. Against that, the defect it closes cost zero over nine days: nobody opened the named file, RESUME_HERE already stated the truth, and the one session that audited the ship-bar got it right without it. On the proposal as written the honest verdict is that this is a tidy-up in a gate's clothing. But the scoped version is a different object. Restricted to the four static instruction files with root-relative resolution, it is ~25 lines, needs ZERO exemptions once three layer-name fragments are fixed in prose, costs ~2 CLAUDE.md lines, and it goes RED on a dated defect this repo actually shipped — which is the bar. Build THAT, fix the line in the same commit, and never let the file list grow to include a scratchpad.
judgements.orderingNote: If it ships, it ships AFTER the one-line fix is already committed, so the first run is green-by-construction and the red is demonstrated by planting the old line back (the brief's doneCriterion) rather than by arriving at a red tree.

judgements.skipSteelman: src/config/CLAUDE.md:7-9 has carried a written admission since 2026-08-24 that labels are review-only and that nothing parses them, and the label is genuinely load-bearing — claimcheck, the twin rule and DIVERGENCES all lean on CONTRACT vs INFERRED. A ~20-line test that makes a doc's own confessed gap impossible to widen is the cheapest possible retirement of a known-weak rule, and the JClaw move it copies (a frozen, named, stale-checked exception store) is the right shape for exceptions.
judgements.bittenUsEvidence: NEVER, AND THE PROPOSED TEST CANNOT CATCH THE ONE CASE ITS OWN DOC NAMES. (1) `grep -niE 'unlabel|missing label|no label|CONTRACT/INFERRED' docs/sessions/-SESSION-LOG.md` -> ZERO hits across the whole log. No logged defect has ever been traced to a missing label. (2) I counted labels vs exports across all 54 src/config/*.ts: 53 of 54 already contain CONTRACT|INFERRED|Spec-fixed. The test is green on arrival over 98% of its scope. (3) The single failing file, ogAi.ts (0 labels, 11 exports), is not an omission — its header says TRANSCRIBED, generated by scripts/payload/transcribeAi.py and byte-checked by tests/ogAiData.test.ts (which exists) with an INDEPENDENT parser. So the gate's first act is to ADD a fourth word to the label vocabulary purely so the existing tree passes. That is widening the rule to fit the evidence, which CLAUDE.md:59 forbids in as many words ('never widen a window to pass'). (4) KILL SHOT: src/config/CLAUDE.md:9 names its own example of the gap — 'ai.ts still ships AI_TIERS unlabeled'. I verified it: AI_TIERS is declared at src/config/ai.ts:29 with no label on it. But ai.ts contains 6 label hits elsewhere in the file, so the proposed PER-FILE test marks ai.ts GREEN. The gate cannot detect the one defect its motivating sentence points at.

standingCost.secondsPerCommit: Negligible — 54 small file reads, well under 100ms. Seconds are not the objection here either.
standingCost.tokensPerTurn: ~2 lines rewritten in src/config/CLAUDE.md (a folder-local file, so loaded only when that folder is in play) plus the new TRANSCRIBED word added to the always-loaded vocabulary. Call it ~40 tok/turn. Small, but paid forever for a check that is already satisfied.
standingCost.linesToMaintain: ~20 lines of test plus an EXEMPT map that starts EMPTY and a stale-check on it — machinery built for a future that has not arrived, which is the definition of speculative abstraction.
standingCost.newFailureModes: (1) FALSE CONFIDENCE, the expensive kind. Per-file granularity means one label word anywhere satisfies a whole file: ogNpcBase.ts = 23 exports / 1 label PASSES, nums.ts = 7/1 PASSES, ogActor.ts = 8/1 PASSES, rng.ts = 7/1 PASSES, ogItems.ts = 5/1 PASSES. After it ships, src/config/CLAUDE.md gets rewritten from the honest 'REVIEW-enforced, not test-enforced' to 'enforced by tests/config-labels.test.ts' — and the repo trades a true warning for a false reassurance across ~60 unlabeled exports. That is strictly worse than the status quo, because today a reader knows to check. (2) The new TRANSCRIBED label becomes an escape hatch: any future unlabeled file can be relabelled TRANSCRIBED in a header comment and go green with nothing verifying that a transcription actually happened. ogAi.ts earns the word because ogAiData.test.ts byte-checks it; nothing in the proposed gate requires that pairing.
standingCost.note: The only version with teeth is per-EXPORT, which the proposal explicitly declines in its own 'honest limit' line.

judgements.simplerVersion: Change nothing in code. src/config/CLAUDE.md:7-9 is already the correct artefact: it states the limitation, names the test that does NOT check it, gives the reproducing grep, and names the live example. An honest warning that a reader can act on beats a green test that certifies 53 files which were never at risk and clears the one file that is. If the gap ever actually bites — a CONTRACT-labelled value turns out to be INFERRED and something downstream trusted it — build the per-EXPORT check then, with that incident as the red to plant.
judgements.why: Zero hits in the session log for the defect class, 53/54 files already green, and the one red is a file whose provenance is stronger than a label (byte-checked by an independent parser) — so the gate's opening move is to widen its own vocabulary to pass. Worst of all, the doc line that motivates it names AI_TIERS in ai.ts, and per-file granularity marks ai.ts green. A gate that cannot see the defect in its own motivating example, over a class that has never once been logged as a cause, is ceremony — and shipping it would license rewriting an honest 'REVIEW-enforced' warning into a false 'test-enforced' claim, which is the exact rot class C2 is supposed to be closing.

judgements.skipSteelman: It is doing real argumentative work: JClaw's 0dfcd451 (six contradicted AGENTS.md claims, drift propagated into a build script and pre-push comments, +96/-43 across three files) is the second independent instance of the class, and it was closed by REVIEW with a staleness stamp already in place. That is what turns 'we found one stale line' into 'this recurs in a repo with more reviewers than we have'. Without it, agent-instructions-1 is a sample of one.
judgements.bittenUsEvidence: Same single instance as agent-instructions-1, restated. Its own ourEvidence field says so verbatim: 'See study-agent-instructions.json / agent-instructions-1: CLAUDE.md:67...'. It contributes no independent defect on our tree, and its own proposal field concedes it is 'not a second gate'.

standingCost.tokensPerTurn: 0 as evidence. NON-ZERO if it is carried on the board as a separate ADOPT, because a verdict list with two ADOPTs for one change is itself a state-schema drift: the next session reads two rows and asks what the second one still owes.
standingCost.linesToMaintain: 0 code. 1 row that must be deleted from the candidate board rather than tracked.
standingCost.newFailureModes: Double-counting in the run's own accounting — a build queue that lists 2 ADOPTs where there is 1 change will report 50% done after shipping 100% of the work, and the next session will go looking for a gate that was never meant to exist.

judgements.simplerVersion: Fold it into agent-instructions-1 as its second-witness paragraph and delete the standalone row. It is evidence, not a deliverable.
judgements.why: DROP as a BUILD ITEM, not as evidence — the distinction matters and I am making it explicitly. It proposes no gate, admits it is merged, and duplicates the only instance we have on our own tree. Its whole value is one sentence inside agent-instructions-1's justification, and keeping it as its own ADOPT row inflates the cluster's apparent yield from one change to two.

docsOnlyCommitRate.command: git log --since=2026-06-17 --format='%H' | while read h; do files=$(git show --pretty=format: --name-only "$h" | /usr/bin/grep -v '^$'); [ -z "$files" ] && continue; printf '%s\n' "$files" | /usr/bin/grep -qvE '\.md$' || echo "$h"; done | wc -l   # denominator: git log --since=2026-06-17 --oneline | wc -l
docsOnlyCommitRate.note: 32.7% of commits take the .githooks/pre-commit docs-only fast path (lines 20-26: if every staged file matches \.md$, print '[gate] Docs-only (markdown) change' and exit 0 BEFORE typecheck/tests/lint). A vitest-hosted instruction-path test therefore does not run on roughly one commit in three. Worse, it is the WRONG one in three: 61 of the 87 md-only commits touched RESUME_HERE.md or a CLAUDE.md, the exact files such a test reads. Two consequences. (a) Direction 'prose edited to name a path that does not exist' is almost always an md-only commit, so it is unprotected outright. (b) Direction 'target deleted while prose stays' is protected only when the deleting commit also stages a non-md file — the real defect (995bb52) qualified ONLY because it also staged .claude/settings.json; .claude/ship-bar.md itself ends in .md, and CLAUDE.md names 7 more .md targets (docs/MASTER_SPEC.md, RESUME_HERE.md, docs/sessions/-SESSION-LOG.md, the three folder CLAUDE.md files, docs/OWNER_PERMISSION_RULING.md) whose md-only rename would be invisible. Net: when the gate does fire it usually fires on a later source commit that did not cause the break, and a blocking gate with broken attribution is the one people learn to --no-verify. Supporting churn figures: RESUME_HERE.md = 164 commits / 991 lines / 84 unique backticked path tokens (34 ending .md), rewritten-not-appended by CLAUDE.md:70; CLAUDE.md = 9 commits / 74 lines / 25 tokens. All the volatility is in the file with none of the defects.

collapses.intoOneChange: ONE commit, two lines of real diff plus a small test. (1) Fix CLAUDE.md:67 to name ~/.claude/settings.json as the ship-bar's source. (2) Fix CLAUDE.md:29-30 to say `src/game/` / `src/core/` / `src/config/` instead of the bare layer fragments — more accurate prose, and it removes 3 of the 4 unresolved tokens in the static set so the test needs no exemption list at all. (3) Add ~25-line tests/instructionPaths.test.ts over exactly CLAUDE.md + src/{core,config,game}/CLAUDE.md, root-relative resolution only. agent-instructions-2 (the stamp) is already superseded by its own brief — the test IS the stamp, machine-checked, and JClaw's stamped block is the one that carried six false claims. harness-evolution-1 becomes the second-witness paragraph in the commit body. Three candidate rows, one change, no exemption file.

notJudged: agent-instructions-2 — verdict SKIP in brief-C2.json, out of scope for this lens (I concur with the skip on fit as well: a date in a comment that nothing verifies costs 1 line per file plus a ritual nobody enforces, and JClaw's own 0dfcd451 is the counter-evidence since all six false claims lived INSIDE the stamped block).
integrity: FILES READ (all read-only, nothing in the repo modified; the only file written is this deliverable): docs/research/runs/jclaw-2026-09-14/refute/brief-C2.json · .githooks/pre-commit · CLAUDE.md (lines 29-31, 55-75, plus full byte/word count) · RESUME_HERE.md (lines 90-100 + token extraction) · src/config/CLAUDE.md (1-20) · src/config/ai.ts (26-29) · src/config/ogAi.ts (1-8) · docs/sessions/-SESSION-LOG.md (grepped, not read whole) · docs/research/HARNESS.md (token extraction only). COMMANDS RUN: git show --name-only/--format on 995bb52 and 45114a0 · git log --all -- .claude/ship-bar.md · git log --since=2026-06-17 with a per-commit name-only md-only classifier (87/266) and the same loop filtered to RESUME_HERE/CLAUDE.md (61) · git log --since=2026-06-17 -- RESUME_HERE.md (164) and -- CLAUDE.md (9) · git grep -n ship-bar over '*.md' · /usr/bin/grep -n over the named files · a per-file backticked-token extractor with `test -e` resolution over the 6 instruction files (132 tokens, 24 unresolved) · label-vs-export counts over all 54 src/config/*.ts · ls on ~/kheshav-code (7 sibling repos, agent-harness present with harness/{chaos,launch-gate,workflows}). COULD NOT CHECK: (1) the actual wall-clock of the current pre-commit run — I did not execute npx vitest, so the '~8s' figure is taken from the prompt, not measured; my per-commit seconds figures are analytic (file sizes and stat counts), not timed. (2) Whether any session was misled by CLAUDE.md:67 in a transcript that never reached git or the session log — my negative finding covers the committed record and the session log only, so it is 'no evidence of harm', which is weaker than 'evidence of no harm'. (3) I did not diff my extractor against the brief's stricter 'ends in a known extension or a slash' filter line by line; my 24/132 and its 16/148 measure slightly different token sets and both are reported rather than reconciled. (4) HOMING QUESTION, partly answered: agent-harness exists at ~/kheshav-code/agent-harness with commit-gate/, hooks/ and harness/launch-gate/ — an established zero-dep Node home that all 7 sibling repos draw from, and 6 of those repos carry their own CLAUDE.md with the same rot exposure. A vitest test inside SSHD gives this check to 1 repo of 7. I did NOT read agent-harness's commit-gate contents, so I cannot say what the port costs; flagging it as the better home on structure alone, and noting the scoped version (root-relative, static files, no exemptions) is exactly the shape that ports cleanly.
